The Story of King Devrati

I bow to Lord Jina, whose eyes are omniscience and who purifies the world, and I write the story of King Devrati, who was lord of Ayodhya.

King Devrati ruled Ayodhya. His queen was named Rakta, and she was exceedingly beautiful. The king was always absorbed in her company, consumed by sensual pleasures. When enemies attacked his kingdom from outside, he paid no heed. He never concerned himself with the state of his realm. Those who abandon dharma and artha — righteousness and material duty — to serve only the desire of the flesh, and who remain ever enslaved to sensual craving, invariably suffer. Such was Devrati's fate.

His ministers found his indifference to governance intolerable. They pleaded with him to take charge of his kingdom, but to no avail. At last, they appointed his son Jaysen as king and banished Devrati and his queen from the country. Cursed be that attachment which reduces honour to dust and brings suffering upon oneself.

Devrati and Queen Rakta wandered into a fearsome forest. The queen was tormented by hunger, and they had not a single grain of food. What could he do? As time passed, the queen grew increasingly restless with hunger. Devrati could not bear to see her suffer — after all, he had abandoned his entire kingdom for her sake. At last he devised a desperate measure: he cut a piece of flesh from his own thigh, cooked it, and fed it to the queen to ease her hunger. To quench her thirst, he drew blood from his arms and, mixing it with a medicinal herb, gave it to her to drink.

They slowly made their way to the banks of the Yamuna. Devrati seated the queen beneath a tree and went to a nearby village to find food. In that place was a small but lovely garden, where a crippled man was drawing water and singing. His voice was extraordinarily sweet, and his singing captivated all who heard it. The melody reached Queen Rakta's ears, and some enchanting power in it so bewitched her that she forgot everything — her husband's sacrifice, her own dignity, all shame. She went to the cripple and offered herself to him without hesitation.

When Devrati returned with food and found his wife in this state, he was shattered. After cutting his own flesh for her, after sacrificing his kingdom and enduring every hardship, she had betrayed him for a mere singer. The depth of his suffering cannot be described. He realised at last the bitter truth — that lust knows no loyalty, and that those enslaved by desire will betray even the one who gave everything for them.

Devrati renounced all attachment and wandered away alone. Through suffering, he gained wisdom. He sought the company of saints, embraced dharma, and at last found peace.

This story teaches that blind attachment to sensual pleasure leads only to ruin. A king lost his throne, his body, and his wife's loyalty — all for the sake of desire. True love is not found in the slavery of the senses but in the purity of the soul.
